## 2026-09-08 Rolling Calendar and Active-plan Information

**Objective:** replace Calendar's fixed previous/today/next navigation with a four-week rolling window, and make Calendar information show only the currently active plan. For past runs, show the Activity record before the active-plan prescription.

**Current stage:** Production release accepted.

**Status:** Complete — **100%**. Engineering implementation, complete QA regression, and the deployed Product Owner walkthrough passed. Production now runs Calendar release `000b38f`.

| Stage | Owner | Status | Evidence / next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requirements and Product scope | Product Owner | Complete | Current-active-plan interpretation confirmed for future and past run information. |
| UX and architecture | UX/UI Designer, Architect | Complete | `docs/design/CALENDAR_ROLLING_WINDOW_UX.md` and `docs/plans/CALENDAR_ROLLING_WINDOW_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`. |
| Implementation | Engineering | Complete | Active-only range/detail work, rolling-window information composition, supporting docs/spec alignment, the deep-link dialog re-open regression fix, and all five QA remediations are complete. |
| Focused validation | Engineering | Passed | Typecheck, full web unit suite (92/92), and targeted Chromium Calendar Playwright coverage (2/2) pass. |
| Full regression | QA | Passed | Production build, typecheck, core 87/87, cloud database 65/65, web 92/92, and all configured Chromium suites passed: local 18, online 8, owner-auth 3. |
| Final live acceptance | Product Owner | Passed | Deployed production walkthrough verified current-week-first four-week Calendar, keyboard rolling, a full past Activity record before active-plan context, future active-plan-only details, and preserved schedule actions. |

**Risks and dependencies:** calendar, activity, handler, and test areas still contain unrelated working-tree changes; preserve them and re-check overlapping files before edits. Scrolling retains exactly four coherent weeks during slow, failed, or out-of-order reads. Date boundaries use the resolved active-plan timezone from first render onward. Calendar distinguishes an unavailable activity read from an empty activity result. Current-active-only plan content may be absent for a historic run when the active plan has no session on that date; the UI represents that truthfully.

**Validation complete:** Calendar browser coverage for wheel/trackpad/touch/keyboard, range announcements, resolved-timezone anchoring, dialog scroll isolation, and error-versus-empty activity state passed. Full regression also passed existing Calendar amendments, Plan activation, Activities, Today, deep links, responsive behavior, accessibility, typecheck, production build, and configured browser suites.

**Production evidence:** deployment `dpl_3Cx11Tqyx67cjLXZpo3GH4Q5UMDr` reached READY with no build errors or runtime error clusters. The deployment retained no unrelated local working-tree changes.

## Current Delivery

## Scope Decisions

- [x] Codex/Second Brain owns AI conversation; app owns agreed structured state.
- [x] Single local athlete, `Africa/Johannesburg`, configurable 06:30 reminder default.
- [x] Manual bounded CSV and one-activity GPX imports.
- [x] Explicit proposal approval and immutable plan versioning.
- [x] Interactive calendar adjustments preserve prescription history.
- [x] In-app Today card separated from Codex recurring-reminder delivery.
- [x] Automatic Garmin sync and automatic post-run review/adaptation deferred to Phase 2.

## Definition of Done

- Every acceptance criterion in the Phase 1 backlog has implementation evidence or an explicitly accepted gap.
- All touched workspaces pass lint, typecheck, unit, integration, and applicable browser tests.
- No private athlete data appears in fixtures, Git, logs, or screenshots.
- API, schema, architecture, UX, roadmap, and progress docs match delivered behavior.
- Product Owner completes the final end-to-end review before the app is presented as Phase 1 complete.

## Next Handoff

Use the accepted Phase 1 journey. Do not begin autonomous review/adaptation or Garmin account integration under this Phase 1 scope.

Accepted Phase 1 gap: imported activities are not matched reliably to prescribed sessions, so the app does not infer workout completion or perform post-run review. Trustworthy matching, review, and adaptation remain Phase 2 work.
